body:
Derek is a Pristinian resident who seeks help finding his sister Rue while trying to protect their vulnerable mother. His frustration with adventurers grows from specific encounters at his home. He later appears again warning the town about gremlins; he remains distinct from the adventurer Derek Belmont.

Prominence and evidence

Prominence unrated. The source footprint alone does not establish the importance of this identity. Consequences, institutional or witness role and relationships need a supported assessment.

Recorded presence combines dialogue volume and span. A brief appearance can still have lasting consequences; missing context is left unrated rather than assigned a low importance.

The notice and the household behind it

Derek posts a missing-person notice for Rue, describing her brown hair and eyes and asking anyone with information to find him. When the adventurers approach, he sarcastically calls himself Robert before admitting that he is Derek and badly stressed. His later explanation makes the joke plain: they have asked the person distributing notices signed Derek whether he is Derek.

He says Rue has failed to return from a morning walk near the forest. She is a year older than him, enjoyed solitude among the trees and had seemed happier after beginning to see Simon. He cannot think of anyone who wanted to harm her. These are the family’s leads at the beginning, not a complete account of what happened.

He suggests mentioning Rody, their childhood dog, so that Rue will know the party comes from him. When asked how a dead dog can miss her, he explains the comfort their mother gave them: that Rody would wait in the afterlife and never forget them. The remembered dog is a family assurance, not an independently observed account of the afterlife.

Helping the search without surrendering his home

At his house Derek finds that Rue’s dress has been washed, then fetches a hairbrush as another possible way to trace her. He gives directions to Simon’s home and reluctantly agrees to accompany the party partway when asked. Trying to help does not mean he has authorized every intrusion into his own house.

When the Dark Raven enters without waiting for permission, he calls out and goes to comfort his frightened mother. He explains that this is why he asked the visitors to wait outside and chooses to stay with her. When the investigation resumes, he is still angry about what happened and tells the next visitors that the masked woman must not return.

He also describes Simon as having changed, including a different air and more pointed ears. His account supplies a lead. It does not by itself prove the cause of that change, identify a new species or make Derek responsible for the party’s conclusions.

What becomes of Rue

The continued search follows Rue’s scent through the First Forest to a grove of birches with faces. One of the trees begins to move and cry, then fights the adventurers. During the confrontation it calls Derek’s name. After the creature falls, the narrator explicitly gives Pappy the knowledge that this was what had become of the missing girl.

The narrator closes the paused-and-resumed quest by establishing that the adventurers tell Derek. The notification happens without a played-out conversation. Rue’s fate and the fact that he is informed are therefore part of the account; Derek’s exact reaction, the family’s later mourning and the whole cause of her transformation remain unrecorded here. The search ends with Rue’s death, and her family is given that answer.

A later warning and an unfinished household history

In a later encounter Derek points toward estates being stripped by gremlins and calls for help. Asked for names, he answers that he did not stop to introduce himself to them and hurries to safety. The sarcasm resembles his first stressed introduction, but the record does not turn that recurrence into a diagnosis or a complete account of his grief.

His mother’s later condition, how the household lives after the news about Rue and Derek’s later whereabouts remain open. The named adventurer Derek Belmont introduces himself separately as a new arrival; the shared first name is no basis for merging their histories.
